title: Reject canonical ID collisions after a legal content filename rename

scope.subject: Filename-independent canonical and legacy identity uniqueness during authoring validation and before new/import writes

research_summary: A disposable CLI fixture reproduces the release gap: rename a valid JSON source without changing its canonical content ID, import the same ID again, then run content:validate. Both commands succeed and the catalogue gains two records with the same canonical target. Reuse the validated Astro payload and existing shared identity-owner validation rather than add an index or database. CLI new/import will use the same owner check before writing any file.

sources.finding: The existing YEIS-backed product retains one native target per canonical personal entry; duplicate IDs would cause order-dependent target resolution.
Astro owns collection intake and source schema. The authoring layer persists a content ID separate from the generated/source filename, so same-ID validation must examine record contents.

search_ladder.conclusion: Reuse canonical destination conventions in the existing YEIS-backed product. Validate identity before it can reach existing placement, search, or navigation.
No ingestion platform change is required; use existing CLI and validated Astro data.
Reuse the existing authoring reference helper and map to validate canonical and legacy IDs by distinct record ownership, including preflight across the existing and incoming catalogs.
The fix is a single O(n) owner check in the shared authoring validator, not a database, owned registry or separate index.

candidates.reason: The same reference checker can reject ambiguous source records regardless of filename for command validation and before writing new/import.

decision.rationale: Use the existing content reference map to track records, not just the canonical ID strings they claim. Reuse that validator for CLI preflight and product build rather than add a second identity subsystem. Preserve file-existence protection and batch rollback.
decision.fallback: For future multi-source importing, normalize all records to the same shared catalog, then apply the same unique reference-owner validation.
